scope: Concurrent start() calls that share one requestId no longer let a competing (rejected) start replace the accepted job's startupDigest or jobId. Ownership is reserved before the first async input stat/read and bound to the job that owns it; store schema is unchanged.

design.reservation: requestId -> {requestId,digest,jobId,claims,waiters}; created before the first async stat/read, never replaced while claimed
design.sameConditionsConcurrent: claims the same reservation; existing src/analysis-jobs.js requestId+fingerprint idempotency still returns one jobId and starts execute at most once
design.differentConditionsInFlight: waits for the in-flight claim to bind a job (ANALYSIS_JOB_REQUEST_CONFLICT) or to be released, then claims; never overwrites the other claim
design.differentConditionsOwned: explicit ANALYSIS_JOB_REQUEST_CONFLICT before any input read
design.digestBinding: onRecord resolves the digest from reservationsByJobId(jobId); the first `running` record emitted inside the synchronous jobs.start call uses the call's own startingReservation
design.rejectedRequestCleanup: a rejected request only decrements its shared claim; it never deletes or mutates another request's reservation, digest or jobId
design.release: forgetReservation(jobId) removes the reservation and its requestId entry only when the map still holds that same object
design.close: drops unowned, unclaimed reservations; owned reservations stay until their terminal record is released
design.failureOnly: when every claimant fails before owning a job, the reservation is deleted; distinct requestId failures do not grow the map
design.storeSchema: unchanged: schemaVersion 1, optional startupDigest, maxRecords 256, maxRecordBytes 8192, no raw paths or result arrays

counterexample.aInput: existing synthetic box fixture (absolute temp path)
counterexample.worker: injected process worker factory that throws immediately (synthetic worker startup failure)
counterexample.beforeFixNote: A-first persisted the B digest (review counterexample reproduced: matchesA false / matchesB true, restart decisions reversed). B-first only appeared correct before the fix because A overwrote B's in-flight slot.
counterexample.afterFixNote: Both dispatch orders: accepted job's record digest is A, 0 records match B, restart classifies A as RESTORED and B as CONFLICT; restored resultAvailable=false.
